To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of breast cancers from Li-Fraumenie syndrome (LFS) patients are ER and/or HER- 2 positive.
most breast cancers in women with LFS are hormone-receptor positive and/or HER2-positive.
most DCIS and invasive cancers in TP53 germlines mutation carriers are hormone receptor and/or HER2 positive.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of cancer, and with the development of new strategies to prevent, diagnose and treat this disease.
understanding the molecular basis of breast cancer in women with LFS and the development of novel therapeutic strategies for these patients.
the study of the molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of breast and other cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the breast cancer phenotype of TP53 mutation carriers is similar to that of the general breast cancer population.
the majority of breast cancers in women with LFS are hormone-receptor-positive, HER-2 positive, and high grade.
breast cancers in women with LFS are more likely than average breast cancers to be hormone receptor positive and HER2 positive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
most of the invasive ductal and DCIS in LFS are ER positive or HER2 positive, or both.
breast cancer in women with LFS is similar to breast cancer in women without LFS, but with a younger age of onset.
breast cancers from LFS women are more likely than expected to be ER/PR positive and HER2 positive, and that this is true for DCIS as well as invasive cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
breast cancers in women with germline TP 53 mutations are often ER/PR and/or HER2 positive, and thus may be responsive to endocrine therapy or trastuzumab.
the phenotype of LFS-associated breast tumors is similar to that of sporadic tumors, which is reassuring to women with LFS who have breast cancer.
breast cancers from women who carry germline mutations of TP53 are more often hormone receptor positive and HER-2/neu positive than previously reported.
